messages:
maria: quick heads-up — ran a targeted perf sweep on the 2k seq workload and saw a weird $/M jump when cache looked 'noisier'
alex: what do you mean by noisy? more evictions?
pat: if kv eviction increases we sometimes fall back from fused/flash to paged on our runtime, that kills tokens/sec
maria: exactly. baseline (steady cache) was ~72k toks/sec, $/M ~8.9. when we hit eviction thrash it dropped to ~42k toks/sec, $/M ~15.3. ran on a g4dn-like instance w/ flash-v2 variant and paged as fallback
bench-bot: [bench output] model=redwood-open-7b seq=2048 batch=8 kernel=flash-v2 kv_hit=0.86 toks/sec=72000 p99_latency=45ms
bench-bot: [bench output] model=redwood-open-7b seq=2048 batch=8 kernel=paged kv_hit=0.40 toks/sec=42000 p99_latency=98ms
ryan: that delta matches our earlier sim but magnitude is bigger than expected. where is the kernel selector kicking in?
daria: selector uses an eviction_threshold + recent_latency heuristic. if KV hit drops below 0.6 for 3 samples we force paged to avoid memory blowups
alex: forcing paged seems too aggressive. evictions can be transient due to prefetch/compactions. we should add hysteresis or a decayed moving average
maria: agreed. i instrumented the selector traces: when compaction runs it spikes evictions for ~200ms and selector flips immediately -> we process a couple hundred concurrent requests on paged then flip back -> oscillation
pat: oscillation is the killer — mixing kernels mid-rollout causes loss of fused kernel batching efficiency and increases kernel launch cost. small bursts multiply into big $/M hits
alex: proposal: 1) add 1s hysteresis window before switching kernels; 2) prefer keeping flash-variant for short seq traffic unless sustained low kv_hit for 5s; 3) cap prefetch concurrency to reduce compaction-triggered evictions
ryan: also add a soft-prefetch throttle: if free_kv_ratio < 0.15, reduce prefetch threads by half. that reduced thrash in my local repro
daria: can we adjust the batching heuristic too? current batcher assumes stable kernel throughput. when kernel flips the optimal batch size changes and we end up with suboptimal micro-batches
maria: i tried a tiny adaptive change: keep per-kernel preferred batch_size and re-evaluate at assignment time. microbench shows this regains ~8% toks/sec after steady state
bench-bot: [mini run] kernel=flash-v2 batch=8 toks/sec=72000 -> keep; kernel=paged batch=4 toks/sec=43000 -> apply; net improvement ~6-9% under mixed traffic
alex: good. action items: - add 1s hysteresis in selector (alex) - implement soft-prefetch throttle (ryan) - per-kernel batch size hints in batcher (pat) - add metric: kernel_flip_rate and kernel_flip_cost ($/M delta) to console (maria)
maria: i'll wire dashboard alerts for kernel_flip_rate > 0.5/min and a cost regression alert if $/M increases >10% vs 10m baseline
pat: i'll drop a draft PR for batcher hints today, include a togglable flag so we can A/B on dedicated fleet
ryan: i'll prototype prefetch throttle and run a 24h soak on staging with realistic chat traces
daria: once we have telemetry, let's run a synthetic where we inject 200ms compaction spikes every 30s and measure steady-state $/M with and without hysteresis
alex: thanks. last note — document the kernel fallback policy in the runtime README and call it out in the console so SREs understand behavior when cost jumps
maria: noted. i'll also add a short explainer in #eng-runtime summary thread after PRs land
pat: thanks everyone. if we can reduce these oscillations we get better tokens/sec and lower $/M — direct customer impact
ryan: leaving a small log snippet here from the repro: ```
[selector] t=17380012.345 eviction_rate=0.18 kv_hit=0.42 -> switch_to=paged
[batcher] t=17380012.402 applied batch_size=8 kernel=flash-v2
[batcher] t=17380012.408 applied batch_size=4 kernel=paged
[selector] t=17380013.112 eviction_rate=0.06 kv_hit=0.81 -> switch_to=flash-v2
```
maria: perfect. closing loop: i'll mark this thread when dashboards/PRs are live. :thumbsup:
